MC	<p>aa2b_5744</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bw, ++, bw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>0a1c_46eb</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1261a1;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1261a1;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1261a1;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973951;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #973951;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect
MC	<p>57fd_af57</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>850e_4950</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, am, ++, am"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>77bd_656b</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c54b8;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3c54b8;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>da6d_fca4</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2e6e23;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1261a1;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1261a1;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>0fcb_8fdd</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13320;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a13320;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13320;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #076788;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ep, ++, ep"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect
MC	<p>40a3_5744</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>1ba3_07e1</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>a2e6_d014</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13320;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a13320;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13320;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c6b63;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973951;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #973951;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>a55d_9166</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7d4094;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7d4094;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>d0f8_a48e</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #586607;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #586607;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #973951;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #973951;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>c2e1_d014</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #076788;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>4f19_3a76</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #586607;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #586607;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c54b8;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3c54b8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. MC	<p>1833_ed0d</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #586607;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #586607;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7d4094;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7d4094;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914601;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>0c65_3de8</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c6b63;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1c6b63;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect
MC	<p>e62c_fa4a</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #076788;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>ec14_7ec1</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914601;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #914601;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914601;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>8874_bef7</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>d4b7_236f</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>5a56_8434</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cd, ++, cd"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>e48b_3620</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2e6e23;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1261a1;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1261a1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>58e5_589f</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>bc27_4628</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914601;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #914601;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914601;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, tw, ++, tw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>7533_5f85</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a76;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pt, ++, pt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>75ae_b22a</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2e6e23;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #903776;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jw, ++, jw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect
MC	<p>8f83_8fdd</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2e6e23;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct
MC	<p>184d_bd68</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6d5d17;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6d5d17;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a76;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a76;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>e4ea_5f85</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #914601;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #914601;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #914601;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13320;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3c54b8;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3c54b8;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct
MC	<p>6a6e_e6f0</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #586607;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #586607;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct
MC	<p>c75a_7011</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #076788;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #076788;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect
MC	<p>bcf6_d014</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #586607;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #586607;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #586607;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6449ab;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6449ab;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, df, ++, df"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect

Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct
MC	<p>f883_236f</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2e6e23;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2e6e23;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7d4094;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7d4094;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>4a9c_1974</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f5406;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f5406;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1261a1;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1261a1;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Correct

A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #903776;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #903776;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. PD, NPD, TT for the other rows</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul></ul><h6>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Determine Linkage</h6><p>The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> has unordered tetrads. A cross is made to study the linkage relationships among two genes.</p> <p>Using the calculation table above, determine the linkage between the two genes.</p>	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> and on the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> chromosome.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #5B2C6F;">NEITHER</strong> <strong>linked</strong> NOR <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #8B0000;">UNLINKED</strong> but may be on either the <strong style="color: #1E40AF;">SAME</strong> or <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Correct	The two genes are <strong style="color: #006400;">LINKED</strong> but are likely on <strong style="color: #D2691E;">DIFFERENT</strong> chromosomes.	Incorrect	The two genes are <strong style="color: #7B3F00;">BOTH</strong> <strong>linked</strong> AND <strong>unlinked</strong>.	Incorrect
MC	<p>02cf_2a81</p> <h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13320;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a13320;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13320;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4d;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #176e4d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype.
